title: The Country of the Quadlings, part 2
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The Lion became quite angry at the laughter caused by the Scarecrow’s mishap, and giving a loud roar that echoed like thunder, he dashed up the hill.
Again a head shot swiftly out, and the great Lion went rolling down the hill as if he had been struck by a cannon ball.

Dorothy ran down and helped the Scarecrow to his feet, and the Lion came up to her, feeling rather bruised and sore, and said, “It is useless to fight people with shooting heads; no one can withstand them.”
“What can we do, then?” she asked.
“Call the Winged Monkeys,” suggested the Tin Woodman. “You have still the right to command them once more.”
“Very well,” she answered, and putting on the Golden Cap she uttered the magic words. The Monkeys were as prompt as ever, and in a few moments the entire band stood before her.
“What are your commands?” inquired the King of the Monkeys, bowing low.
“Carry us over the hill to the country of the Quadlings,” answered the girl.

“It shall be done,” said the King, and at once the Winged Monkeys caught the four travelers and Toto up in their arms and flew away with them. As they passed over the hill the Hammer-Heads yelled with vexation, and shot their heads high in the air, but they could not reach the Winged Monkeys, which carried Dorothy and her comrades safely over the hill and set them down in the beautiful country of the Quadlings.
“This is the last time you can summon us,” said the leader to Dorothy; “so good-bye and good luck to you.”
“Good-bye, and thank you very much,” returned the girl; and the Monkeys rose into the air and were out of sight in a twinkling.

The country of the Quadlings seemed rich and happy. There was field upon field of ripening grain, with well-paved roads running between, and pretty rippling brooks with strong bridges across them. The fences and houses and bridges were all painted bright red, just as they had been painted yellow in the country of the Winkies and blue in the country of the Munchkins. The Quadlings themselves, who were short and fat and looked chubby and good-natured, were dressed all in red, which showed bright against the green grass and the yellowing grain.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened when the Lion charged the hill?
options: He went rolling down as if struck by a cannon ball
He drove the Hammer-Heads back behind the rocks
He reached the top before they could stop him
He was caught and held by many heads at once

questions.prompt: Per the passage, who suggested calling the Winged Monkeys?
options: The Tin Woodman
The Scarecrow
The Lion
Dorothy herself

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy command the Monkeys to do?
options: Carry them over the hill to the Quadling country
Destroy the Hammer-Heads on the hillside
Take them straight across the desert
Fetch Glinda to come and help them

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what colour was everything in the Quadling country?
options: Bright red
Bright yellow
Deep blue
Emerald green

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the Quadlings like?
options: Short, fat, chubby, and good-natured
Tall and thin, with pointed hats
Armless, with heads that shoot out
Made entirely of painted china

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Lion conclude about the fight?
options: It is useless to fight people with shooting heads
The Hammer-Heads could be beaten with the axe
They should attack all together next time
The hill could be climbed by another path

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could the Hammer-Heads not stop the flight?
options: Their heads could not reach the flying Monkeys
They had used up their strength on the Lion
The Monkeys flew round the hill instead
Glinda had forbidden them to interfere

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Monkey King tell Dorothy at parting?
options: That this was the last time she could summon them
That they would come again whenever she called
That the Golden Cap must be given to Glinda
That they would carry her over the desert next

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does vexation mean?
options: Angry frustration
Sudden terror
Loud amusement
Quiet sorrow

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Force fails on the hill, and the last call of the Cap carries them over
The Lion defeats the Hammer-Heads after a long fight
The travellers give up and return to the forest
Glinda sends the Winged Monkeys to fetch them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion feel after his roll down the hill?
options: Rather bruised and sore
Entirely unhurt
Too badly hurt to walk
Angrier than before

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did Dorothy call the Monkeys?
options: Put on the Golden Cap and said the magic words
Blew the little whistle from the Queen of the Mice
Sent the Scarecrow to the top of the hill
Shouted their names across the valley

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what ran between the fields of grain?
options: Well-paved roads
Narrow muddy tracks
Rows of red fences
A wide green river

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how quickly did the Monkeys answer?
options: As prompt as ever, in a few moments
Only after a long delay
Not until the following morning
They did not come at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what made the Lion charge in the first place?
options: He was angry at the laughter over the Scarecrow
He believed his new courage made him safe
Dorothy had asked him to clear the way
He wanted to reach Glinda before dark

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does in a twinkling mean?
options: In an instant
Reluctantly
Without a sound
One at a time

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: The last of the Cap's power lifts them into a rich red country
A battle on the hillside that the travellers finally win
The Monkeys refuse a third command and fly away
The party walks around the hill and finds the Quadlings
